# Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects. Initiative Statute.
## Summary
Amends California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) to expedite environmental review for certain projects (including most housing, transportation, water, and health projects) by setting deadlines to complete environmental review and resolve lawsuits challenging project approvals.
**Fiscal Impact:** Initial costs for state and local governments, likely in the high tens of millions of dollars—potentially exceeding $100 million—annually, partly covered by fees.
Uncertain, potentially more significant positive or negative longer-term fiscal effects.
...
## What your vote means
## Yes
A YES vote on this measure means: Certain public and private projects would be eligible for new project review and court challenge procedures.
For example, new procedures would tighten time limits for environmental review and reduce the scope of what courts can consider when reviewing legal challenges.
## No
A NO vote on this measure means: Public and private projects would continue to use existing project review and court challenge procedures.

### Official Title and Summary
### Prepared by the Attorney General
## Healthcare Insurance. Rate Changes. Initiative Statute.
- Requires changes to health insurance rates, or anything else affecting the charges associated with health insurance, to be approved by Insurance Commissioner before taking effect.
- Provides for public notice, disclosure, and hearing on health insurance rate changes, and subsequent judicial review.
- Requires sworn statement by health insurer as to accuracy of information submitted to Insurance Commissioner to justify rate changes.
- Does not apply to employer large group health plans.
- Prohibits health, auto, and homeowners insurers from determining policy eligibility or rates based on lack of prior coverage or credit history.
### Summary of Legislative Analyst's Estimate of Net State and Local Government Fiscal Impact:
- Increased state administrative costs to regulate health insurance, likely not exceeding the low millions of dollars annually in most years, funded from fees paid by health insurance companies.

PROP
45
MODIFIES ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW FOR CERTAIN PROJECTS. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Amends California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) to expedite environmental review for certain projects (including most housing, transportation, water, and health projects) by setting deadlines to complete environmental review and resolve lawsuits challenging project approvals. Fiscal Impact: Initial costs for state and local governments, likely in the high tens of millions of dollars—potentially exceeding $100 million—annually, partly covered by fees. Uncertain, potentially more significant positive or negative longer-term fiscal effects. Supporters: California Children’s Hospital Association; California Water Association; California Council for Affordable Housing Opponents: Coalition for Clean Air; CA Environmental Voters; Physicians for Social Responsibility, LA; National Wildlife Federation
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Certain public and private projects would be eligible for new project review and court challenge procedures. For example, new procedures would tighten time limits for environmental review and reduce the scope of what courts can consider when reviewing legal challenges.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: Public and private projects would continue to use existing project review and court challenge procedures.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
The failing status quo is making California unaffordable. Prop. 45 fixes our broken system and lowers our high cost of living by cutting red tape to build housing, water, schools, hospitals, clean energy, and wildfire prevention faster—while maintaining California’s strong environmental protections. Vote YES for a more affordable California. YESonProp45.com
CON
PROPOSITION 45 LIMITS ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC REVIEW OF PROJECTS BUILT IN YOUR COMMUNITY. It guts The California Environmental Quality Act—flipping California law to protect corporate profits over public health and our air and water. Prop. 45 won’t lower your costs: its utility and corporate funders profit while taxpayers pay more. VOTE NO.

PROP
45
MODIFIES ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW FOR CERTAIN PROJECTS. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Amends California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) to expedite environmental review for certain projects (including most housing, transportation, water, and health projects) by setting deadlines to complete environmental review and resolve lawsuits challenging project approvals. Fiscal Impact: Initial costs for state and local governments, likely in the high tens of millions of dollars—potentially exceeding $100 million—annually, partly covered by fees. Uncertain, potentially more significant positive or negative longer-term fiscal effects. Supporters: California Children’s Hospital Association; California Water Association; California Council for Affordable Housing Opponents: Coalition for Clean Air; CA Environmental Voters; Physicians for Social Responsibility, LA; National Wildlife Federation
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Certain public and private projects would be eligible for new project review and court challenge procedures. For example, new procedures would tighten time limits for environmental review and reduce the scope of what courts can consider when reviewing legal challenges.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: Public and private projects would continue to use existing project review and court challenge procedures.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
The failing status quo is making California unaffordable. Prop. 45 fixes our broken system and lowers our high cost of living by cutting red tape to build housing, water, schools, hospitals, clean energy, and wildfire prevention faster—while maintaining California’s strong environmental protections. Vote YES for a more affordable California. YESonProp45.com
CON
PROPOSITION 45 LIMITS ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC REVIEW OF PROJECTS BUILT IN YOUR COMMUNITY. It guts The California Environmental Quality Act—flipping California law to protect corporate profits over public health and our air and water. Prop. 45 won’t lower your costs: its utility and corporate funders profit while taxpayers pay more. VOTE NO.

The poll was conducted by the Public Policy Institute of California:
“The tight margins, after campaigning by both sides, show the measure is a tricky one for Californians who value environmental protections but are frustrated by the state’s high housing and utility costs, [PPIC’s] Baldassare said.
In the same survey data, more than half of Californians named the cost of living, inflation and housing costs as the most important issues facing the state.
The tight polling reflects divides around the proposal that have played out in some unusual ways.
Though a majority of Republican voters favors Prop.
45, 41% remain opposed in the latest PPIC poll, and some county-level Republican parties have split from the state central committee, which endorsed it.

**DOWNWARD ARC —** Where a campaign stands matters less than where it’s headed — and less than a week from the election, major ballot initiatives are losing ground.
The trendlines are troubling for Proposition 40, which would impose a one-time wealth tax on California’s billionaires, and for Proposition 45, which would streamline environmental reviews for construction projects.

Yes on Prop. 45 leads by a thin margin
October 27, 2026 / in News, Insights & Research (https://www.probolskyresearch.com/category/news-insight-and-research/) / by Probolsky Research (https://www.probolskyresearch.com/author/probolsky-research/)
Probolsky Research regularly conducts election and public policy polling for public interest. We have released these results for California Proposition 45 on the November ballot for public interest . The company has no client in the race nor any affiliation with the respective campaigns.
“There is a clear gender divide on Prop. 45. Men support the measure 51% to 36%. Women oppose it 42% to 36%,” explained Dr. Adam Probolsky, president of Probolsky Research. “The Bay Area has some of the highest housing costs, yet that’s the region where the highest opposition shows up.”
Media Contact: Dr. Adam Probolsky, 949-697-6726

How this is built
Proposition 45 is forecast as a environment and energy measure whose Yes vote leans to neither party . Comparable measures from 2018 to 2024 set how far its Yes share moves with California 's partisanship, and each county moves with its own age, education, race and density mix as well as its 2024 presidential vote, so no two counties share a margin by default. How it reached the ballot moves it further. Polls then pull the forecast toward them by recency and size, after splitting undecided voters two to one for No. Sources: elections.cdn.sos.ca.gov (https://elections.cdn.sos.ca.gov/ccrov/2026/june/26179jj.pdf), growsf.org (https://growsf.org/news/2026-07-02-14-state-measures/), ppic.org (https://www.ppic.org/publication/ppic-statewide-survey-californians-and-their-government-september-2026/), cpapracticeadvisor.com (https://www.cpapracticeadvisor.com/2026/09/23/california-voters-back-billionaire-tax-and-measures-that-could-block-it-new-poll-finds/190410/). Yes on Prop. 45 leads by a thin margin
October 27, 2026 / in News, Insights & Research (https://www.probolskyresearch.com/category/news-insight-and-research/) / by Probolsky Research (https://www.probolskyresearch.com/author/probolsky-research/)
Probolsky Research regularly conducts election and public policy polling for public interest. We have released these results for California Proposition 45 on the November ballot for public interest . The company has no client in the race nor any affiliation with the respective campaigns.
“There is a clear gender divide on Prop. 45. Men support the measure 51% to 36%. Women oppose it 42% to 36%,” explained Dr. Adam Probolsky, president of Probolsky Research. “The Bay Area has some of the highest housing costs, yet that’s the region where the highest opposition shows up.”

Proposition 45 is forecast as a environment and energy measure whose Yes vote leans to neither party . Yes on Prop. 45 leads by a thin margin
October 27, 2026 / in News, Insights & Research (https://www.probolskyresearch.com/category/news-insight-and-research/) / by Probolsky Research (https://www.probolskyresearch.com/author/probolsky-research/)
Probolsky Research regularly conducts election and public policy polling for public interest. We have released these results for California Proposition 45 on the November ballot for public interest . The company has no client in the race nor any affiliation with the respective campaigns.
“There is a clear gender divide on Prop. 45. Men support the measure 51% to 36%. Women oppose it 42% to 36%,” explained Dr. Adam Probolsky, president of Probolsky Research. “The Bay Area has some of the highest housing costs, yet that’s the region where the highest opposition shows up.”
Media Contact: Dr. Adam Probolsky, 949-697-6726
Probolsky Research is a nonpartisan Latina- and woman-owned market and opinion research firm with corporate, election, government, and nonprofit clients.

## Summary
Amends California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) to expedite environmental review for certain projects (including most housing, transportation, water, and health projects) by setting deadlines to complete environmental review and resolve lawsuits challenging project approvals.
**Fiscal Impact:** Initial costs for state and local governments, likely in the high tens of millions of dollars—potentially exceeding $100 million—annually, partly covered by fees.
Uncertain, potentially more significant positive or negative longer-term fiscal effects.

## What your vote means
## Yes
A YES vote on this measure means: Certain public and private projects would be eligible for new project review and court challenge procedures.

PROP
45
MODIFIES ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW FOR CERTAIN PROJECTS. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Amends California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) to expedite environmental review for certain projects (including most housing, transportation, water, and health projects) by setting deadlines to complete environmental review and resolve lawsuits challenging project approvals. Fiscal Impact: Initial costs for state and local governments, likely in the high tens of millions of dollars—potentially exceeding $100 million—annually, partly covered by fees. Uncertain, potentially more significant positive or negative longer-term fiscal effects. Supporters: California Children’s Hospital Association; California Water Association; California Council for Affordable Housing Opponents: Coalition for Clean Air; CA Environmental Voters; Physicians for Social Responsibility, LA; National Wildlife Federation
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Certain public and private projects would be eligible for new project review and court challenge procedures. For example, new procedures would tighten time limits for environmental review and reduce the scope of what courts can consider when reviewing legal challenges.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: Public and private projects would continue to use existing project review and court challenge procedures.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
The failing status quo is making California unaffordable. Prop. 45 fixes our broken system and lowers our high cost of living by cutting red tape to build housing, water, schools, hospitals, clean energy, and wildfire prevention faster—while maintaining California’s strong environmental protections. Vote YES for a more affordable California. YESonProp45.com
CON
PROPOSITION 45 LIMITS ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC REVIEW OF PROJECTS BUILT IN YOUR COMMUNITY. It guts The California Environmental Quality Act—flipping California law to protect corporate profits over public health and our air and water. Prop. 45 won’t lower your costs: its utility and corporate funders profit while taxpayers pay more. VOTE NO.

Proposition 45 is forecast as a environment and energy measure whose Yes vote leans to neither party . Comparable measures from 2018 to 2024 set how far its Yes share moves with California 's partisanship, and each county moves with its own age, education, race and density mix as well as its 2024 presidential vote, so no two counties share a margin by default. How it reached the ballot moves it further.
